en: Two neighbouring precincts in inner-south Sydney, about one kilometre apart, are being rebuilt as high-density neighbourhoods, yet they are told as two different stories. Green Square, a 278-hectare former industrial area, is presented by the City of Sydney as Sydney's "oldest industrial heartland" that "has transformed into a vibrant, sustainable and connected community", with a planned 63,000 residents and about 22,000 jobs (City of Sydney, n.d.). Waterloo's public housing estate, about 2,000 dwellings on 18 hectares, has been called "terrible" and "no longer fit for purpose" by ministers and local members, and long overdue for renewal (Zanardo et al., 2024). Its planning proposal places it "1 kilometre north of Green Square Town Centre" (NSW Land and Housing Corporation [LAHC], 2021, §1.1.2). This essay argues that the two precincts sit inside one planning frame, that of a global city, but are separated by two different stories about their past, and that the planning documents then use the first precinct as a built-form precedent for the second. The two descriptions already map onto course concepts: Green Square's is a language of heritage and potential, Waterloo's a language of deficiency and obsolescence, and Zanardo et al. (2024) and Sisson (2024) read the second through the concept of the reputational gap. The cost of transplanting a model onto a place that is already inhabited falls on the people who live there.

q: 这一段只说“本文补什么”，你想不想把“已有研究已经做了什么”写得更具体？
en: The core argument of this essay, that one planning frame hosts two different stories about the past, is built from the four units of the course. From the introductory unit it takes the global city (Sassen, 1991) and the view of urbanisation as a terrain of struggle over land and housing; from the housing unit, the conflict between housing as home and as real estate (Madden & Marcuse, 2016); from the segregation unit, vicious circles and neighbourhood effects (Tammaru et al., 2021); and from the gentrification unit, the rent gap, social mixing and state-led gentrification (Lees, 2008; Yrjänä, 2026). The evidence is policy and planning documents, the consultation record, and three academic studies of Waterloo by Sisson (2024), Zanardo et al. (2024) and Wynne and Rogers (2021). Because these studies already use some of the same concepts, each section below states which concepts they use and what the contrast with Green Square adds. Sisson and Zanardo et al. both describe a "reputational gap" between the estate's present and its idealised future; none of the three studies mentions Green Square in its text. The contribution of this essay is therefore the comparison, and the test of what the idealised future leaves out.
zh: 本文的核心论点——同一个规划框架容纳了两种不同的“过去”叙事——是按课程的四个单元建立的。导论单元提供全球城市（Sassen, 1991）和“城市化是围绕土地与住房的斗争场域”这一视角；住房单元提供“住房作为家”与“住房作为房地产”之间的冲突（Madden & Marcuse, 2016）；隔离单元提供恶性循环与邻里效应（Tammaru et al., 2021）；绅士化单元提供租金差、社会混合与国家主导的绅士化（Lees, 2008; Yrjänä, 2026）。证据包括政策与规划文件、咨询记录，以及三项关于 Waterloo 的学术研究：Sisson (2024)、Zanardo et al. (2024) 和 Wynne & Rogers (2021)。由于这些研究已经用到部分相同的概念，下文每一节都会交代它们用了哪些概念，以及与 Green Square 的对比能增加什么。Sisson 和 Zanardo 等人都描述了公屋区“现状”与“被理想化的未来”之间的“声誉差距”；三项研究都没有提到 Green Square。因此，本文的贡献在于这一对比，以及检验那个“被理想化的未来”遗漏了什么。

q: 个人经历这一句要不要保留？保留的话放在引言还是结论？
“福利承诺 vs 全球城市雄心”要不要在引言里讲得更具体？
en: The author's personal note is not evidence, but it explains why reputation matters to the argument that the two precincts are told as two different stories. The author has lived near Redfern, knows the area's reputation well, and still enjoyed walking its streets; the gap between the reputation and the experience is where this essay began. Sections 2 to 5 follow the four course units: the global city, development strategies, reputation, and the promise of mixing and return. Behind the comparison lies a tension between a welfare commitment, the aim of using social housing to break disadvantage, and a global-city ambition, to which the conclusion returns. Throughout, claims about intent are avoided, and the interpretation is marked as interpretation, because documents can show what a policy says and what it uses as a reference, but not what the authors of the policy hoped. In concept terms, a gap between reputation and experience is what the reputational gap names when the reputation is the official one, and what Sennett's pair of building and dwelling names when the experience is the resident's; this application is mine. This keeps the argument about two stories and a transplanted model within what the documents can support.
zh: 作者的个人经历不是证据，但它说明了为什么名声这个问题对“两个片区被讲成两个不同的故事”这一论点很重要。作者曾住在 Redfern 附近，很清楚这个地区的名声，却依然喜欢在那里的街上散步；名声与体验之间的落差，是本文的起点。第 2 至第 5 节依次对应课程的四个单元：全球城市、开发策略、声誉，以及混合与回迁的承诺。比较的背后有一种张力：一边是福利承诺，即用社会住房来打破劣势，另一边是全球城市的雄心，结论部分将回到这一点。全文避免对意图下判断，并把解释明确标为解释，因为文件能说明一项政策写了什么、用什么作参照，却无法说明政策制定者的期望。从概念上说，名声与体验之间的落差，当名声是官方的名声时，就是声誉差距所指的东西；当体验是居民的体验时，就是 Sennett 的“建造与栖居”这一对概念所指的东西；这一应用是我的。 这使得关于两个故事和被移植模式的论证保持在文件所能支撑的范围之内。

q: “两块战场”这个说法要不要保留？还是换成更学术的表达？
en: The introductory unit supplies the frame that lets the two precincts be read together, which is the first step of the argument that they sit in one planning frame. Sassen (1991) describes a small number of cities, such as New York, London and Tokyo, as hubs that manage and coordinate the global economy, and also as sites of deep inequality and social change; Brenner and Schmid (2021), as presented in the course, treat urbanisation as a global process and a terrain of struggle over land, housing and basic services. Neither concept is applied to Sydney in the lectures, so the application here is an interpretation. It follows the logic of both: if a city competes as a global economic hub, land becomes the place where that ambition meets the residents who already live on it. For this essay, land and housing are the terrain, and Waterloo and Green Square are two fields of the same struggle.
zh: 导论单元提供了能把两个片区放在一起阅读的框架，这是“它们处在同一个规划框架之内”这一论点的第一步。Sassen (1991) 把纽约、伦敦、东京等少数城市描述为管理和协调全球经济的枢纽，同时也是深刻不平等与社会变迁的场所；Brenner & Schmid (2021)（课程中介绍）把城市化看作一个全球过程，是围绕土地、住房和基本服务的斗争场域。讲义并没有把这些概念用到悉尼，所以这里的应用是一种解释。它遵循两者的逻辑：如果一座城市以全球经济枢纽的身份竞争，那么土地就成了这种雄心与已经住在那里的居民相遇的地方。对本文而言，土地与住房就是斗争场域，Waterloo 和 Green Square 则是同一场斗争的两块战场。

q: 首句里“Green Square 被点名、Waterloo 没有”是铺垫下一段的伏笔，你想放在这一段还是下一段？
en: Sydney's own planning documents state the global-city ambition explicitly, and in them Green Square is named while Waterloo is not, which makes Green Square the precinct whose place in the shared planning frame is documented. The 2014 metropolitan strategy, subtitled "a strong global city, a great place to live", defines a Global Economic Corridor that "extends from Macquarie Park through the Sydney CBD to Port Botany and Sydney Airport" and "generates over 41 per cent of the NSW Gross State Product" (NSW Planning and Environment, 2014, p. 44; the subtitle is as catalogued by the National Library of Australia). The map of the corridor (Figure 15, p. 45) marks Green Square as a strategic centre, the strategy lists it among Sydney's strategic centres, and its Central subregion section commits to facilitating the Green Square Town Centre project, "comprising around 4,000 dwellings and 90,000m² of commercial and retail area" (p. 113). In this document the concept of the global city appears as economic competitiveness: jobs, output and infrastructure. Green Square is therefore an explicit part of the global-city plan.
zh: 悉尼自己的规划文件明确写出了全球城市的雄心，在这些文件里 Green Square 被点了名而 Waterloo 没有，这使 Green Square 成为在共同规划框架中的位置有文件记载的那个片区。2014 年的大都市战略副标题是“一个强大的全球城市，一个宜居之地”，它界定了一条全球经济走廊：“从 Macquarie Park 经悉尼 CBD 到 Port Botany 和悉尼机场”，并“贡献 NSW 逾 41% 的州内生产总值”（NSW Planning and Environment, 2014, p. 44；副标题据澳大利亚国家图书馆目录）。走廊地图（图 15，p. 45）把 Green Square 标为战略中心，战略文本也把它列入悉尼的战略中心，中部分区部分则承诺推进 Green Square Town Centre 项目，“约 4,000 套住宅和 90,000 平方米商业零售面积”（p. 113）。在这份文件里，全球城市的概念表现为经济竞争力：就业、产出和基础设施。因此，Green Square 是全球城市规划中被明确点名的一部分。

q: 你想不想自己看一眼 Figure 15，再决定这一段的措辞（“落在带内”还是“紧邻”）？
en: Waterloo's place in that frame is less direct. The 2014 strategy does not name Waterloo anywhere; it mentions Redfern and the Central to Eveleigh area. On the corridor map, which is at a small scale and does not label Waterloo, the yellow band runs from the CBD south through Green Square towards the airport, and Waterloo lies between the CBD and Green Square, so it falls inside the band by position. This is the present author's reading of the map. Wynne (2018) reads the estate the same way: she writes that Waterloo "sits within this global economic corridor" and alongside the Green Square "strategic centre", citing the same strategy. I did not find the phrase "urban renewal corridor", which she also uses, in the strategy's text, so the corridor claim should be attributed to her interpretation and to the map, not to a statement in the plan. The link between Waterloo and the global-city frame is therefore plausible and geographical, but made by the reader.
zh: Waterloo 在这个框架里的位置则没那么直接。2014 年的战略文件通篇没有点名 Waterloo，只提到 Redfern 和 Central to Eveleigh 地区。走廊地图的比例尺很小，也没有标注 Waterloo，但黄色走廊带从 CBD 向南经过 Green Square 通向机场，而 Waterloo 正好在 CBD 与 Green Square 之间，所以按位置它落在这条带内。这是本文作者对地图的读法。Wynne (2018) 也这样理解：她写道 Waterloo“位于这条全球经济走廊之内”，紧邻 Green Square 这个“战略中心”，并引用了同一份战略。我在战略正文里没有找到她同样使用的“urban renewal corridor”这一措辞，因此走廊的说法应归于她的解读和这张地图，而不是规划原文的陈述。所以，Waterloo 与全球城市框架的联系是合理的、基于地理位置的，但是由读者建立的。

q: “框架偏向前者”是判断还是描述？你要不要补一条文献支撑？
en: Wynne's (2018) ethnography shows what the shared frame means for the residents of Waterloo, who live inside the second of the two stories. She writes that municipalities approach the global-city ambition "by opening up real estate markets for global investment and large-scale development", and that inner-city public housing residents "are aware that they, too, are seen as being in the way of the city's transformation". Sennett (2018) distinguishes the building of cities from the dwelling in them, and defines the city as a settlement in which strangers are likely to meet. In Wynne's account, the government sees the estate's modernist towers "as signifying anachronistic welfare state and city planning ideals", while a resident says of them: "they're good to live in. These buildings were built for eternity". Sennett's pair does not appear in Sisson, in Zanardo et al., or in Wynne and Rogers, so it is one of the concepts this essay adds. Building and dwelling are in tension in Waterloo, and the global-city frame favours the first.

q: “不全盘接受”这一步很关键，你要不要说得更具体（接受哪部分、不接受哪部分）？
en: Sassen's emphasis on inequality inside the global city gives the shared frame a critical edge that the planning documents lack, and it bears on the first of the two stories. Wynne (2018) draws on Harvey (2008) to describe the global city as one in which "the rich displace the poor through a process of 'accumulation through dispossession'", and she argues that in the discourse of the global city "investment, finance and growth are key, while notions of home, attachment to place and the local are absent". These are strong claims, and the present essay does not adopt them wholesale: the 2014 strategy does not say that it aims to displace anyone, and the Waterloo redevelopment adds social homes. What the critical reading contributes is a question about what the frame measures, since a plan that counts jobs and output will not register attachment to place. That question explains why the same planning frame can contain both a precinct without residents, which it can plan cleanly, and an estate full of residents, which it can renew only by relocating them.
zh: Sassen 对全球城市内部不平等的强调，给这个共同框架增添了规划文件所缺乏的批判锋芒，它与两个故事中的第一个有关。Wynne (2018) 借助 Harvey (2008)，把全球城市描述为“富人通过‘剥夺式积累’的过程置换穷人”之地，并认为在全球城市的话语里，“投资、金融和增长是关键，而家、对地方的依恋和本地性则缺席”。这些是很强的判断，本文并不全盘接受：2014 年的战略没有说它的目的是置换任何人，Waterloo 的再开发也增加了社会住房。这种批判性读法所贡献的，是一个关于“这个框架在衡量什么”的问题，因为一个以就业和产出计数的规划，是不会登记对地方的依恋的。这个问题解释了为什么同一个规划框架里既可以有一个没有居民、可以干净规划的片区，也可以有一个住满了居民、只能通过让他们搬迁才能更新的公屋区。

en: The housing unit asks whether housing is a home or an asset, and the Waterloo case, which the essay sets against Green Square, shows that the two answers compete. Madden and Marcuse (2016, p. 4) describe "a conflict between housing as lived, social space and housing as an instrument for profitmaking – a conflict between home and real estate", and Aalbers (2016) defines financialisation as the growing role of financial motives, markets and actors in shaping housing. Sisson (2024) speaks of "neoliberal asset management logics" in public housing policy and of the aim of "value for money"; Zanardo et al. (2024) speak of land values, "highest and best use" and asset recycling; Wynne and Rogers (2021) speak of "land value uplift". q: “需求 vs 消费”的对比你要不要用 Waterloo 与 Green Square 各一个具体例子支撑？
en: The housing question that Ilmonen frames in the lecture, as it changes from the industrial to the post-industrial city, helps to show how the two precincts carry two different stories. In the industrial city housing is a need, the needs are quantitative and the households are working class; in the post-industrial city housing is consumption, the needs are qualitative and the households are middle class and increasingly diverse. The Waterloo estate belongs to the first period: it was built by the Housing Commission from the late 1940s, and towers such as Matavai and Turanga were designed for people on pensions (Zanardo et al., 2024). Green Square belongs to the second, and the City describes it in the language of choice, as "a great place to live, work and visit" (City of Sydney, n.d.). This reading is my application of the lecture's framework, since neither Zanardo et al. nor the City uses it. It suggests that the two precincts embody two answers to the housing question, and that moving the second model onto the first site replaces housing as need with housing as consumption, in the same place and for different households. This is the sense in which the precedent is a transplant and not only a design.

q: “机制”一句很重要，你要不要单独拎出来做一个小标题？
en: Waterloo's side of the comparison rests on its strategy, which is stated in the 2016 social housing strategy, Future Directions. Its first action is to "fast-track redevelopment of its social housing portfolio" in partnership with the private sector through Communities Plus, and to "ensure large redevelopments target a 70:30 ratio of private to social housing to enable more integrated communities" (NSW Government, 2016, p. 9). Sites were chosen for land value. Zanardo et al. (2024) report that Communities Plus "major projects" targeted large estates "with high land values, close proximity to employment and economic growth areas, good transport connections", and a history of low-density zoning that allowed intensification; Waterloo "comfortably met" these criteria, and the decision to build a metro station there "further enhanc[ed] land values and ensur[ed] financial feasibility". Wynne and Rogers (2021) likewise link the decision to redevelop to the station and to transit-led "land value uplift". The mechanism is that private development pays for the replacement of social housing, which community housing providers then manage, drawing on exemption from the goods and services tax and on tenants' eligibility for Commonwealth Rent Assistance (Zanardo et al., 2024). In this strategy, the estate's value as land is what makes its renewal affordable to the state, which is the basis on which the Green Square model can be transplanted onto an inhabited site.

en: The numbers show what the land-based strategy does to the share of social housing, which is the first measure of who bears the cost of the transplanted model. Waterloo South currently has about 750 social dwellings (NSW Government, 2024). The 2026 project plan is for about 3,300 homes, including about 1,050 social, 700 affordable and 1,550 private homes (Homes NSW, 2026). The number of social homes therefore rises by about 300, but they fall from the great majority of the existing homes to about a third of the total. In 2023 the proportion of social and affordable housing for the project was raised from 34 to 50 per cent (NSW Government, 2023). Zanardo et al. add that social housing in Australia is a highly "residualised" tenure, with a small stock and tight eligibility. The concept of residualisation appears in their account, and the figures illustrate it: even where the stock grows, its place in the whole shrinks. The strategy increases the stock while reducing the weight of public housing in the neighbourhood, which is what treating housing as land produces and where the cost of the transplanted model first shows.

en: Green Square, the precinct used as the precedent, follows a different strategy. It is new construction on former industrial land, led by the City and the state, and the City's page reports that total private development cost will be about A$22 billion, against A$1.8 billion for local public infrastructure, of which the City itself spends about A$710 million including land (City of Sydney, n.d.). White (2014), an author from the City, lists the challenges as flooding, traffic, infrastructure funding and fragmented land ownership, and describes planning mechanisms used "to encourage developers and the state government to partner in the city's vision". The City's page does not mention affordable or social housing. The urban design study for Waterloo South, however, tabulates Green Square Town Centre as having 104 social and affordable dwellings out of 3,308, about 3 per cent (Turner Studio & Turf, 2020, App. 6, p. 463; the figures are read from a scanned table and should be checked against the page). The strategy is the same in logic, since public money prepares land for private housing, but it is applied to land with no inhabitants and results in a very small share of social housing.
zh: Green Square 这个被用作先例的片区，采取的是另一种策略。它是在前工业用地上新建，由 City 和州政府主导。City 的页面显示，私人开发总造价约 220 亿澳元，本地公共基础设施约 18 亿澳元，其中 City 自己的支出约 7.1 亿澳元（含土地）（City of Sydney, n.d.）。来自 City 的作者 White (2014) 把挑战列为洪水、交通、基础设施资金和零散的土地所有权，并描述了用来“鼓励开发商和州政府参与城市愿景”的规划机制。City 的页面没有提到可负担或社会住房。但 Waterloo South 的城市设计研究把 Green Square Town Centre 列为 3,308 套住宅中有 104 套社会与可负担住房，约占 3%（Turner Studio & Turf, 2020, App. 6, p. 463；数字取自扫描表格，需对照原页核对）。这一策略在逻辑上是相同的，即公共资金为私人住房准备土地，但它用在没有居民的土地上，结果是社会住房的比例很小。

q: 这一段是“对立证据”，你想放在这里还是集中放在第 4 节的对立段？
en: A fair account of the transplanted model must also credit what the Waterloo strategy delivers. The 2023 government release says that 70 new social homes at the Waterloo Metro Quarter and over 100 social homes at Elizabeth Street in Redfern will allow some Waterloo South tenants to be relocated in the local area (NSW Government, 2023). At the same time, Zanardo et al. (2024) note that the new social housing is managed by community housing organisations instead of the state housing agency, which shifts both the funding route and the form of management. In Zanardo et al.'s terms the sector is residualised, so even a modest net gain matters to a small stock, which is why the strategy cannot be dismissed as a loss. The point for this essay is not that the strategy fails to add homes, which it does not, but that the way it adds them ties the future of social housing to the value of the land.
zh: 对被移植模式的公允叙述，还必须承认 Waterloo 策略所带来的东西。政府 2023 年的新闻稿说，Waterloo Metro Quarter 的 70 套新社会住房和 Redfern 的 Elizabeth Street 逾 100 套社会住房，将使 Waterloo South 的一部分租户可以在本地安置（NSW Government, 2023）。同时，Zanardo 等人 (2024) 指出，新的社会住房由社区住房组织而不是州住房机构管理，这改变了资金路径，也改变了管理形式。按 Zanardo 等人的说法，这个部门是残余化的，所以对一个很小的存量而言，即使是适度的净增加也很重要，这就是为什么不能把这项策略简单地当作损失。本文的重点不是说这项策略没有增加住房，它确实增加了，而是说它增加住房的方式把社会住房的未来与土地的价值绑在了一起。

q: “反对的不是图书馆或公园”是一个重要的限定，你要不要放到更醒目的位置？
en: The design study also records what the Green Square precedent does carry, and a fair account of the transplanted model should credit it. Among the key lessons drawn from Green Square Town Centre is "Start with the Spaces": the early commitment to providing and delivering community infrastructure is described as a highlight of the Town Centre's planning (Turner Studio & Turf, 2020, App. 6, p. 462). White (2014) likewise describes civic buildings, water recycling and place-making initiatives as part of the City's contribution. If the precedent carries a commitment to public facilities ahead of private housing, it is worth transferring, and the objection of this essay is not to the library or the parks. The objection is to what the precedent leaves behind. In the course's terms, public facilities serve the home side of the conflict between home and real estate; this application of the lecture's concepts is mine. Green Square began as a place without a resident community, so, as far as I could read them, the lessons listed for it concern how to build for newcomers, and not how to rebuild around the people who are already there.

q: “不证明排斥”是你之前明确要求的措辞，你要不要保留这样的限定？
en: The two strategies can be compared on one measure, the share of social housing, which shows how the second story differs from the first, but the comparison has limits. Waterloo South plans 30 per cent of residential floor area as social housing (LAHC, 2020, §5.1.7), while the Green Square Town Centre is recorded at about 3 per cent social and affordable. The scopes differ: the City's own target in Sustainable Sydney 2030 is that, by 2030, 7.5 per cent of housing in the whole local area will be social and 7.5 per cent affordable rental housing (City of Sydney, n.d.-b), and the 3 per cent refers to one town centre. The difference does not show that Green Square excludes disadvantaged groups by design, for which this essay has no evidence; it shows that the precinct is a market-led one, while the Waterloo precinct is one where the state owns the land and has to reconcile redevelopment with the people on it. The ratio is the measure behind the social mix discussed in the segregation and gentrification units: 30 per cent and 3 per cent are two different mixes. The policy implication is that the same document treats the market-led precinct as a precedent for the state-owned one, a point examined in Section 5.

en: The segregation unit supplies the vocabulary in which the story about Waterloo is told, and the policy documents use the same vocabulary in plain terms. Massey and Denton (1988) define segregation as the degree to which groups live separately in different parts of the urban environment. Tammaru et al. (2021, p. 68) explain its reproduction through "the sorting of people into concrete activity sites" and "the contextual effects people experience at these activity sites", and add that the way social housing is distributed, clustered in certain neighbourhoods or spread evenly, shapes this sorting; "advantage breeds advantage and disadvantage breeds disadvantage" (p. 69). The lecture develops this into a chain from spatial clustering of disadvantage, through neighbourhood effects and selective mobility, to wider segregation and immobility across generations (Rosengren, 2026). The NSW documents speak in these terms, so the concepts are present in the policy rather than imposed by the course, and the question of this section is how that language is used to tell the story about Waterloo that the Green Square story is later set against.

q: 首句“支撑故事的诊断”和末句“缝隙”要不要呼应得更明显？
en: Future Directions gives the diagnosis that supports the story told about Waterloo, in these words. About 40 per cent (41,000 dwellings) of social housing in NSW is in concentrated estates, and "while a range of social housing estates function relatively well, many estates experience high levels of crime, unemployment, domestic violence, tenancy management problems, poor educational outcomes and associated child protection issues. These experiences can be passed on through multiple generations, reinforcing the cycle of disadvantage" (NSW Government, 2016, p. 24). The Productivity Commission (2017, p. 205) writes that "a social environment can develop that compounds the effects of disadvantage, and increases the chance that disadvantage is passed on from one generation to the next", citing Vinson (2009). The remedy in the passage on page 24 is Place Plans, which aim at education, training and jobs, and it does not mention demolition. But the same strategy proposes the 70:30 redevelopments "to enable more integrated communities" (p. 9), and a minister's statement on the same page presents Communities Plus as "at the forefront of encouraging people in social housing to be aspirational, not generational". Diagnosis and remedy are in different sections, and the link between them is made in the ministerial language and in the research that follows. This gap between diagnosis and remedy is where the story about Waterloo's reputation takes hold.

q: 这一段是全文最靠近已有文献的一段，你想怎样标明“这是 Sisson 的，不是我的”？
en: Sisson (2024) analyses how that story is built, and his critique has four parts. First, he calls the concept of neighbourhood effects behind "concentrated disadvantage" one that "controversially" locates cause in the estate; second, he notes that tenants are thereby represented, "sympathetically (albeit condescendingly)", as "passive agents whose lives are structured by their noxious environment"; third, he argues that the concentration itself resulted from "targeting, market rents and funding declines", so the focus on the place obscures structural causes; and fourth, he shows how this stigma legitimises renewal, especially where public housing stands on valuable real estate and the state wants "value for money". He draws on Wacquant's concept of territorial stigma and on Kallin's reputational gap, and he describes Communities Plus as articulating reputational gaps "between an estate's supposedly deficient present and its idealized future" in order to pursue rent gaps. Zanardo et al. (2024) extend this: Waterloo suffers several stigmas, in housing and social policy, in planning and design, and in the media, and it is selectively presented as obsolete although there is no evidence that it is among the worst public housing in NSW. These two studies have already made the central argument about Waterloo's reputation, so the contribution of this essay is to set that story against the one told about Green Square.
zh: Sisson (2024) 分析了这个故事是如何构建的，他的批评有四个部分。第一，他称“邻里效应”这一支撑“劣势集中”的概念“有争议地”把原因放在住宅区上；第二，他指出租户因此被“同情地（尽管居高临下地）”表述为“生活被有害环境塑造的被动行动者”；第三，他论证劣势集中本身是“定向分配、市场租金和经费下降”造成的，所以把焦点放在地方上掩盖了结构性原因；第四，他说明这种污名如何为更新提供正当性，尤其是在公屋占着有价值的房地产、国家想要“物有所值”的地方。他借助 Wacquant 的地域污名概念和 Kallin 的声誉差距，并描述 Communities Plus 是在表达“住宅区所谓有缺陷的现状与其被理想化的未来之间”的声誉差距，以便追求租金差。Zanardo 等人 (2024) 进一步指出：Waterloo 承受着住房与社会政策、规划设计、媒体三个层面的多重污名，而且它被选择性地呈现为过时的，尽管没有证据表明它是 NSW 最差的公共住房。这两项研究已经完成了关于 Waterloo 声誉的核心论证，所以本文的贡献，是把那个故事与讲 Green Square 的故事对照起来。

q: 三种读法的顺序（善意→批判→条件）是否需要调整？
en: The phrase "aspirational, not generational" shows how the diagnosis in the story about Waterloo turns into a theory of the tenant. In Future Directions it is a goal for the whole system: "We want to encourage residents in social housing to be aspirational, not generational" (NSW Government, 2016, p. 4); and a minister later joins it to a condition, namely that many new social housing units will be used "to trial innovative programs that link housing assistance to participation in education, training and local employment opportunities" (p. 9). Three readings are possible. It can be read as an honest aim of opening routes out of poverty. It can be read, with Sisson, as locating the cause in the tenant's lack of aspiration, which resembles what Arthurson and Jacobs (2009, as cited in Sisson, 2024) call a social integrationist discourse, in which disadvantage is blamed on isolation and on the conditioning of aspirations by concentration. And it can be read as a step towards conditionality, linking the right to a home to behaviour. The course literature does not analyse this phrase, so the mapping to Sisson's categories is mine. I found no counterpart to it in the official descriptions of Green Square, which speak of place rather than of the aspirations of its residents.
zh: “有志向，而非世代相传”这句话显示了关于 Waterloo 的故事里的诊断如何变成对租户的一种理论。在 Future Directions 里，它是整个体系的目标：“我们希望鼓励社会住房居民有志向，而不是世代相传”（NSW Government, 2016, p. 4）；一位部长后来又把它与一个条件连在一起，即许多新的社会住房将被用来“试验把住房援助与参加教育、培训和本地就业机会挂钩的创新项目”（p. 9）。可以有三种读法。一种是把它读作开辟脱贫路径的诚实目标。一种是随 Sisson 把它读作把原因放在租户缺乏志向上，这类似于 Arthurson & Jacobs (2009，转引自 Sisson, 2024) 所说的“社会整合话语”：把劣势归咎于孤立，以及集中居住对志向的塑造。还有一种是把它读作走向附带条件的一步，把获得住房的权利与行为挂钩。课程文献没有分析这句话，所以与 Sisson 分类的对应是我的。我在对 Green Square 的官方描述里没有找到与之对应的说法，那些描述谈的是地方，而不是居民的志向。

q: 这一段决定论证是否公允，你想把它放在 Sisson 之前还是之后？
en: A fair reading of the story told about Waterloo, which the argument about two stories depends on, must also include the counter-evidence. The mechanism behind the diagnosis is not an invention of politicians. The segregation lecture itself treats neighbourhood effects as a real mechanism, with objective effects on education and services and subjective effects on perceptions of the neighbourhood; and the Productivity Commission cites research on children in lower-income neighbourhoods. Sisson's critique is therefore best read as a critique of attribution and remedy, namely that the problem is placed in the estate and the remedy is its redevelopment, not as a denial that concentration of disadvantage can matter. This distinction matters for the essay, because the contrast with Green Square asks where the "problem" is placed, not whether disadvantage is real. A defence of the policy can claim support in the course's own concepts, and the argument here has to answer it. The argument about the transplanted model has to answer that defence.
zh: 对 Waterloo 这个故事的公允阅读——关于两个故事的论证依赖于它——还必须包括对立证据。这一诊断背后的机制并不是政治家的发明。隔离讲义本身就把邻里效应当作一种真实的机制，对教育和服务有客观影响，对邻里的观感有主观影响；Productivity Commission 也引用了关于低收入街区儿童的研究。因此，Sisson 的批评最好理解为对归因与对策的批评，即把问题放在住宅区里、把对策定为拆除重建，而不是否认劣势集中可能产生影响。这个区分对本文很重要，因为与 Green Square 的对比问的是“问题”被放在哪里，而不是劣势是否真实。对这项政策的辩护可以在课程自己的概念里找到支持，本文的论证必须回应它。 关于被移植模式的论证必须回应这一辩护。

q: 这一段要不要保留？它不确立任何东西，但解释了为什么土地价值成了资金来源。
en: The lecture on segregation in a retrenching housing regime asks whether the setting of the Waterloo story, a state that funds social housing less directly, is also found in Sydney, and the evidence is partial. Rosengren (2026) describes a drift in Finland from proactive housing policy towards reactive social policy, in which supply-side housing subsidies were replaced by demand-side ones and responsibility for segregation was delegated to local levels. I could not verify that the housing regime in NSW has retrenched in the same way, and the claim is not made here. Two pieces of evidence point in a similar direction. Sisson (2024) writes that the concentration of disadvantage in public housing resulted from targeting, market rents and funding declines. Zanardo et al. (2024) describe a funding route for new social housing that works through community housing providers' tax exemption and tenants' eligibility for federal rent assistance, which is a demand-side instrument. The Finnish parallel is therefore suggestive and not established, and it bears on the argument about the transplanted model because a regime in which the state funds social housing less directly is one in which land value becomes the more important source of funds.
zh: 关于紧缩的住房制度下的隔离的那场讲座问：Waterloo 这个故事的背景——国家较少直接为社会住房出资——在悉尼是否也存在，而证据是不完整的。Rosengren (2026) 描述了芬兰从积极的住房政策转向被动的社会政策的漂移：供给侧住房补贴被需求侧补贴取代，隔离的责任被下放到地方层面。我无法证实 NSW 的住房制度以同样的方式收缩了，本文也不作这一断言。有两项证据指向类似的方向。Sisson (2024) 写道，公共住房中劣势的集中是由定向分配、市场租金和经费下降造成的。Zanardo 等人 (2024) 描述了新建社会住房的一条资金路径：它通过社区住房组织的税收豁免和租户领取联邦租金援助的资格来运作，而联邦租金援助是一种需求侧工具。因此芬兰的对照是提示性的、而非已被确立的，它与关于被移植模式的论证有关，因为在国家较少直接为社会住房出资的制度里，土地价值就成了更重要的资金来源。

q: 你之前问过“没找到是不是说明没有污名”，现在的写法是否满意？
en: Green Square offers the contrast to the story about Waterloo, and its limits must be stated. The City's description of Green Square is of heritage and promise: "a rich past and an exciting future", an "industrial heartland" turned into a "vibrant, sustainable and connected community" (City of Sydney, n.d.), and White (2014) places the area's problems in flooding, transport, funding and land ownership. I did not find a source that describes Green Square before redevelopment as a stigmatised place, but the search was limited, and an absence in a few sources is not proof of an absence of stigma. A more defensible reading follows from the concept of the reputational gap, which Sisson and Zanardo et al. take from Kallin (2017): the gap between an imagined potential and a devalued present exists in both places, but in Green Square the devalued thing is land and infrastructure, while in Waterloo it is people and buildings. The difference may follow from the fact that there were no residents on the Green Square site to be stigmatised. This reading is my interpretation. It keeps the contrast between the two stories without claiming that Green Square is stigma-free, and it does not require evidence of exclusion.
zh: Green Square 提供了与 Waterloo 故事的对照，但必须说明其局限。City 对 Green Square 的描述是遗产与前景：“丰富的过去和令人期待的未来”，“工业核心地带”变成“充满活力、可持续、互联互通的社区”（City of Sydney, n.d.），而 White (2014) 把该地区的问题放在洪水、交通、资金和土地所有权上。我没有找到把 Green Square 改造前描述为被污名化之地的资料，但这次搜索有限，几份资料里的缺席并不证明没有污名。更站得住的读法来自声誉差距这一概念，Sisson 和 Zanardo 等人从 Kallin (2017) 那里借用了它：想象的潜力与被贬低的现状之间的差距在两个地方都存在，但在 Green Square，被贬低的是土地和基础设施，而在 Waterloo，被贬低的是人和建筑。这一差别可能源于 Green Square 的场地上没有居民可以被污名化。这一读法是我的解释。它保留了两个故事之间的对比，并不声称 Green Square 没有污名，也不需要排斥的证据。

q: White 是 City 员工，你要不要在正文里提醒读者这是官方视角？
en: White's (2014) account of Green Square's past supplies the first of the two stories in its own words. The area's industrial heritage "dates back to 1815"; by the early 1900s it was "the largest industrial municipality in Australia", with over 500 factories and 22,238 workers; and then, as manufacturing left South Sydney, there followed "this process of decline", a period as an area for waste processing, and a land use that is now "light industrial", generally "up to two storeys high" with a large footprint. White also names the Gadigal people of the Eora nation as the area's traditional owners, so the narrative is not without people, but they stand at the beginning of the story. The account has the same shape as the one told about Waterloo, a deficient present set against a better future, but its subject is a land use and its infrastructure, and not a population: the decline is of factories and waste sites, and the future is a town centre. This fits the reputational gap as Sisson and Zanardo et al. use it, and it shows that the gap can be opened by describing land. The contrast with Waterloo lies in the object of the story, and the object is where the cost of renewal falls.

q: “连接社区”这句话有两种读法（善意/排斥），你想怎么处理？
en: The policy implication for the argument about the transplanted model is that stigma and redevelopment reinforce each other in Waterloo. The urban design study for Waterloo South states that "the challenge for Waterloo South is to link this community with the established economic centres by increasing links either north towards Redfern or south to Green Square" (Turner Studio & Turf, 2020, Part 1, PDF p. 84). Here the residents are described as a community to be connected, and Green Square is named as one of the destinations. The diagnosis of concentration and the aim of mixing support one another: the first defines the problem and the second defines the remedy. If the problem is the place, the remedy is to change the place, and the land value released in doing so pays for it. This is the pattern which Sisson (2024) criticises, and the Green Square contrast shows its other side: where the land is empty, no such account of the problem is needed.

en: The gentrification unit brings the earlier concepts together and asks who bears the cost of the transplanted model. Stein (2019, p. 41), as quoted in the lecture, defines gentrification as the process by which capital is reinvested in neighbourhoods, and poorer residents and their cultural products are displaced and replaced by richer people and their preferred aesthetics and amenities; it is "planned by the state, produced by the developers and consumed by the condo crowd". Smith's (1979) rent gap is the disparity between potential ground rent and the rent capitalised under the present land use. Davidson (2018) extends the concept to new-build development and to indirect displacement; Lees (2008) criticises social mixing as a positive packaging of gentrification; and Yrjänä (2026) shows in Helsinki how anti-segregation policy can serve state-led gentrification, with a reputational gap and a subsidy gap. In the Waterloo literature the label is already in use: Wynne (2018) writes of "the state-led gentrification of their neighbourhood", and Wynne and Rogers (2021) discuss gentrification and cite Lees and Davidson. The contribution of this section is therefore to test what the precedent and the promise mean for the residents.

en: The rent gap is the part of the account of the two stories that is closest to the documents. Zanardo et al. (2024) show that Waterloo was selected for its land value, that the metro station "further enhanc[ed]" it, and that the estate has a "significant reputational gap, created through denigration of its present use and idealization of its future use", which they connect to ground rents potentially received through partial privatisation and redevelopment. The rent gap thus explains why the state wants Waterloo's land, and the contrast shows that in Green Square the same gap was closed without anyone to displace.

q: 这一段的结论是“未知”，你要不要保留？它有价值，但读者可能觉得没结论。
en: Davidson's (2018) account of new-build gentrification offers a way to ask whether the two precincts are linked by more than a planning document, and so whether the cost of the transplant spreads beyond the estate. Following Davidson and Lees (2005), as summarised in the course, it identifies four elements of gentrification: the reinvestment of capital, the social upgrading of a locale by higher-income groups, a change in the landscape, and the direct or indirect displacement of low-income groups. Against the view that new building on vacant land is only residentialisation, Davidson argues that indirect displacement can occur when an area becomes harder for poorer people to stay in. Social upgrading and direct displacement cannot be judged for a site that had almost no residents. Indirect displacement would depend on whether neighbouring areas are affected, and I found no study of whether rents or displacement in Waterloo or Alexandria have been shaped by Green Square. The concept therefore leaves an open question that matters for the argument: whether the precinct used as a precedent for Waterloo also acts on Waterloo's surroundings. The documents show a planned link, in the design study's aim of connecting the estate to Green Square, and not an observed effect.

q: 这一段是正反两面各占一半，你想让它偏向哪一边？
en: Social mixing is the promise that is supposed to make the transplanted model acceptable to Waterloo's residents, and the evidence on it is divided. Future Directions links the 70:30 target to "more integrated communities", and the Waterloo plans use the language of tenure-blind design, which Sisson and Zanardo et al. both note. The consultation report for the estate found "strong support for social, affordable and private housing to be evenly distributed across the whole of the Waterloo precinct", but "mixed views" on mixing within individual buildings: those in favour felt it "would be more equitable and help support social cohesion", while those against stressed the difficulty of meeting the diverse needs of the different residents in one building (Elton Consulting, 2019). Lees (2008) supplies the sceptical case from the unit: mixing policies are one-directional, they do not in practice produce interaction between old and new residents, and they can erode the support networks that concentration provides. The Elton report shows that residents themselves hold both views. The mixing argument is therefore a legitimate position, and its weakness for the argument about the cost of the transplanted model is that its promise has not been shown to reach the people it names.

q: 这一段是课程阅读，你要不要把“芬兰 vs 悉尼”的对照单独拎成一个小节？
en: Yrjänä's (2026) study of Helsinki, a course reading, offers a parallel that shows what is specific to the Waterloo story. In two stigmatised outer neighbourhoods, Mellunkylä and Meri-Rastila, a new urban renewal model launched in 2020 aimed to deconcentrate disadvantaged and ethnic-minority groups and to change the tenure mix, and Yrjänä argues that the language of anti-segregation, with its statistical measures, gives moral cover to state-led gentrification. She uses the reputational gap, which Sisson and Zanardo et al. also use, and the subsidy gap, in which the state first pays the economic difference in order to de-risk private investment. The structure of the argument, a stigmatised place, a state that owns the land and a policy of mixing, is the same in both cities. The difference lies in the welfare context: Finland's mixing policy draws on a large social housing sector and a long record of social mixing (Rosengren, 2026), while Waterloo's draws on a small, residualised sector, which is why its mixing has to be paid for by private development. The subsidy gap also raises a question about the cost of the transplanted model, namely whether the state's investment in the metro station works as such a first payment; I offer this as an analogy, and I have not found it documented.
zh: Yrjänä (2026) 对赫尔辛基的研究是一项课程阅读，它提供了一个对照，显示出 Waterloo 这个故事的特殊之处。在两个被污名化的外围社区 Mellunkylä 和 Meri-Rastila，2020 年启动的新的城市更新模式旨在“去集中化”弱势群体和族裔少数群体并改变权属结构，Yrjänä 认为，反隔离的语言及其统计指标为国家主导的绅士化提供了道德掩护。她用到了声誉差距（Sisson 和 Zanardo 等人也用到了）和补贴差距，即国家先垫付经济差额，以便为私人投资去风险。论证的结构——被污名化的地方、拥有土地的国家、混合政策——在两座城市是相同的。差别在福利背景：芬兰的混合政策依赖于庞大的社会住房部门和长期的社会混合实践（Rosengren, 2026），而 Waterloo 的混合依赖于一个小的、残余化的部门，这就是它的混合必须由私人开发来买单的原因。

q: 调查数字只通过报道知道，你要不要在正文里更明显地标明这一点？
en: For residents, who carry the cost of the transplanted model, the redevelopment is already experienced as a loss of place before any building is demolished. Wynne and Rogers (2021) call this emplaced displacement: displacement that occurs in the absence of physical relocation, and they find that "timeline uncertainty is a key problem" in the experience of residents. Rogers and Wynne (2020) summarise their ethnography of 2010–2017 by saying that "even the threat of being moved has already done significant damage to residents' relationship with their homes and community", at an estate of about 4,000 people in 2018. The consultation found that participants "expressed a strong connection to the Waterloo social housing estate and local area" and stressed that it should remain "an authentic place with its own character" (Elton Consulting, 2019). A 2023 survey of 320 public housing tenants, reported in the press, found that 58 per cent feel part of their community, that 45 per cent would move out if given the opportunity, that 59 per cent feel unsafe walking in the neighbourhood after dark, and that only 33 per cent think their voice can be heard (South Sydney Herald, 2024). These findings show both attachment and dissatisfaction, and they fit the concept of emplaced displacement: the place is valued and the future of the place is uncertain. The cost of the transplanted model is already being carried by those who live there.

q: 这一段是数据，你想把数字做成一个小表放在正文里吗？
en: Census figures at the suburb level help to place the two areas, but they cannot settle the comparison of the two stories. In 2021 the Waterloo suburb had 16,379 people and a median weekly household income of A$2,028; 72.7 per cent of occupied dwellings were rented and 91.1 per cent were flats. Zetland, which includes Green Square Town Centre, had 12,622 people and a median weekly household income of A$2,192; 70.5 per cent were rented and 92.5 per cent were flats (Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2021a, 2021b). Two things follow. Green Square is not an area of owner-occupiers: it is overwhelmingly rented apartments, as Waterloo is, so a contrast based on tenure would mislead. And the near-identical profiles show that suburb data dilute the estate, which had about 4,000 residents in 2018 in a suburb of more than 16,000 (Rogers & Wynne, 2020). In the segregation unit's terms, such data would be used to measure the dissimilarity between areas (Rosengren, 2026), and here they cannot, because both suburbs are dominated by rented apartments. The comparison therefore has to rest on the estate's own sources, such as the consultation and the tenant survey, so that the cost to its residents can be seen.
zh: 郊区层级的人口普查数字有助于定位这两个地区，但无法裁定对这两个故事的比较。2021 年 Waterloo 郊区有 16,379 人，家庭周收入中位数 2,028 澳元；72.7% 的住宅被出租，91.1% 是公寓。包含 Green Square Town Centre 的 Zetland 有 12,622 人，家庭周收入中位数 2,192 澳元；70.5% 被出租，92.5% 是公寓（Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2021a, 2021b）。由此可以得出两点。Green Square 不是自住业主的地区：它和 Waterloo 一样，绝大部分是出租公寓，所以以权属为基础的对比会产生误导。而且，两者几乎相同的概貌表明，郊区数据稀释了公屋区——它在 2018 年约有 4,000 居民，而所在郊区有一万六千多人（Rogers & Wynne, 2020）。用隔离单元的话说，这类数据本可用来测量地区之间的相异程度（Rosengren, 2026），而在这里做不到，因为两个郊区都以出租公寓为主。因此，这一比较必须建立在公屋区自己的资料之上，如咨询和租户调查，这样才能看到居民所承担的代价。

q: 这一段是全文最重要的解释，你想让它的限定放在段首还是段尾？
en: The precedent is where the comparison with Green Square becomes concrete. The planning proposal for Waterloo South states that its urban design study "provides a detailed analysis of built form precedents throughout the broader Green Square area" (LAHC, 2020, §5.1.7). In that study, Green Square Town Centre is one of three local "comparative density case studies", alongside Central Park and Crown Square, which are said to show the factors that lead to "great urban places" within Australia, and a further page compares Waterloo and Zetland together, at 143 people per hectare at present and 247 in the future (Turner Studio & Turf, 2020, App. 6, pp. 462–464). On the other side, the residents in Wynne's (2018) study fear that "we'll have something soulless like what's around Danks St" and the paper reports that "global city" renewal projects, "such as at Green Square, are viewed by residents as unattractive places to live". The documents therefore show that Green Square is used as a precedent, and the residents show that they do not want its result. I read the two together as Green Square functioning for Waterloo as an imagined future, but no document says so, which is the transplant at the centre of this essay, but no document says so, and this is an interpretation to be tested rather than a finding.
zh: 先例是与 Green Square 的比较变得具体的地方。Waterloo South 的规划建议书说，其城市设计研究“详细分析了更广泛的 Green Square 一带的建筑形态先例”（LAHC, 2020, §5.1.7）。在这项研究里，Green Square Town Centre 是三个本地“可比密度案例”之一，另两个是 Central Park 和 Crown Square，据说它们展示了在澳大利亚“好的城市地方”的形成因素；另有一页把 Waterloo 和 Zetland 合在一起比较，现有 143 人/公顷，未来 247 人/公顷（Turner Studio & Turf, 2020, App. 6, pp. 462–464）。另一方面，Wynne (2018) 研究中的居民担心“我们会得到像 Danks St 一带那样没有灵魂的东西”，论文还报告说，“全球城市”更新项目，“如 Green Square，被居民视为不吸引人的居住地”。所以，文件显示 Green Square 被用作先例，居民则显示他们不想要它的结果。这正是本文所关注的那个移植，但没有哪份文件这样说，这是有待检验的解释，而不是发现。

q: Sisson & Ruming 我只知道题目，你要不要取得全文后再决定这一句写什么？
en: The promise of return is the point on which the claim about the cost of the transplanted model can be tested, and it cannot yet be tested. The state's commitment is that existing tenants "will be relocated in small stages … and will be given the right to return once the renewal is complete", and that new social homes at the Waterloo Metro Quarter and in Redfern would let some be rehoused locally (NSW Government, 2023). Because the redevelopment is staged over many years, whether tenants return cannot be known now. Advocacy groups argue that the right of return should be granted now and that those relocated report different experiences from those the government publicises (City Hub, n.d.). What can be said is what the concept of emplaced displacement implies: that a right to return does not remove the displacement that occurs while waiting, and that "return" needs defining, to the same place, the same dwelling or the same community. Sisson and Ruming (2024) have developed new measures of the social housing lost and added in estate renewal, which indicates how the promise of return, and so the cost to residents, could be checked once data exist.
zh: 回迁的承诺是可以检验“被移植模式的代价”这一论点的地方，但目前还无法检验。国家的承诺是，现有租户“将分小批搬迁……并在更新完成后获得回迁的权利”，Waterloo Metro Quarter 和 Redfern 的新建社会住房可以让一部分人在本地安置（NSW Government, 2023）。由于再开发要分阶段进行许多年，租户是否回迁，现在无从得知。倡导团体认为回迁权应当现在就给予，并称被搬迁者讲述的经历与政府宣传的不同（City Hub, n.d.）。能说的是“在地失所”这一概念所蕴含的：回迁的权利不能消除等待期间发生的失所，而且“回迁”需要被定义——回到同一个地方、同一套住宅，还是同一个社区。这表明一旦有了数据，回迁的承诺——也就是居民所承担的代价——如何可以被核查。

q: “两个方向”的写法很稳，你要不要给出自己的倾向？
en: The policy question is whether these arrangements strengthen or weaken the gentrification dynamic that the transplanted model brings, and the evidence points both ways. They strengthen it where the funding model makes land value the condition of renewal, where the precedent is a market-led precinct, and where the promise of mixing replaces a measure of who benefits. They weaken it where the number of social homes rises, where the combined social and affordable share was raised to 50 per cent in 2023, and where local rehousing is offered (NSW Government, 2023). A defender can fairly say that more social homes are better than the status quo and that the alternative to value capture has been no renewal at all. The limits of that defence are that the share of social housing falls while the stock rises, that the precedent gives little weight to those who live there, and that the promise of return has not been tested. These policies do not simply benefit or harm the residents; they move the cost of the model onto them in ways that the documents do not count.
zh: 政策问题是，这些安排究竟是强化还是削弱了被移植模式所带来的绅士化动力，证据指向两个方向。在资金模式让土地价值成为更新的条件、先例是市场主导的片区、混合的承诺取代了对“谁受益”的衡量时，它们强化了这种动力；在社会住房数量增加、2023 年社会与可负担合计比例提高到 50%、并提供本地安置时，它们削弱了这种动力（NSW Government, 2023）。辩护者可以公平地说，更多的社会住房好于现状，而价值捕获的替代方案是根本没有更新。这一辩护的局限在于：存量上升时占比在下降，先例很少给予居住者分量，回迁的承诺尚未经受检验。这些政策并不简单地使居民受益或受害；它们把这种模式的成本以文件没有计入的方式转移到了居民身上。

en: The comparison of Waterloo and Green Square shows that the issue is not whether one precinct is better than the other, but what happens when a model is transplanted onto a place that is inhabited. Both precincts belong to a global-city plan, as the introductory unit's concepts and the 2014 strategy suggest; their development strategies differ in who owns the land and who pays; their reputations are produced through different stories of the past, which the segregation unit's concepts of neighbourhood effects and the reputational gap help to read; and the planning documents use the market-led precinct as a precedent for the state-owned one. This is the central argument of the essay. The existing studies of Waterloo, Sisson (2024) and Zanardo et al. (2024), establish that stigma legitimises renewal; the contrast added here shows what the idealised future is made of, and that its social cost is not in the documents' accounts.
zh: Waterloo 与 Green Square 的比较表明，问题不在于哪个片区更好，而在于把一种模式移植到有人居住的地方会发生什么。两个片区都属于一份全球城市规划，这是导论单元的概念和 2014 年战略所提示的；它们的开发策略不同，差别在于谁拥有土地、谁来付费；它们的声誉由不同的过去叙事所生产，隔离单元的邻里效应与声誉差距概念有助于解读这一点；规划文件则把市场主导的片区当作国有土地片区的先例。这是本文的核心论点。关于 Waterloo 的既有研究——Sisson (2024) 和 Zanardo 等人 (2024)——已经确立了污名为更新提供正当性；本文增加的对比则显示了那个被理想化的未来是用什么构成的，以及它的社会代价不在文件的账目之内。

q: 统计方法要不要在脚注里说明（按英文关键词计数，不含参考文献）？
en: A count of the concepts in the existing literature shows where this essay's argument about the two stories adds to it. In the English text of the three Waterloo studies, territorial stigma appears 46 times in Sisson and not at all in the others; the reputational gap appears once in Sisson and twice in Zanardo et al.; the rent gap appears once, in Sisson; words built on "gentrif-" appear 11 times in Wynne and Rogers, who also use the global city five times and introduce emplaced displacement; and social mixing or tenure-blind design appears in all three. Green Square does not appear in any of the three, and neither does Sennett's pair of building and dwelling. Wynne's (2018) paper uses the global city more than fifty times and mentions Green Square three times, without making the comparison. These counts are a rough guide to emphasis, not to argument, since a concept can be used without the term. They do show that stigma and the reputational gap are already well covered, and that the places where this essay adds to the literature are the Green Square contrast, the building and dwelling distinction, and the test of the promise of return.

q: “悉尼是不是福利城市”你原来不确定，现在的写法（证据不支持强福利）是否可以接受？
en: The tension between a welfare commitment and a global-city ambition, which sits behind the claim that one planning frame hosts two stories, appears more complicated than a simple opposition. Zanardo et al. (2024) describe social housing in Australia as highly residualised, a small stock with tight eligibility, so Sydney is not a strong welfare city on this evidence, although the extent of its welfare provision more broadly is not something this essay has examined. Within that small sector, the model of Communities Plus uses the land value of estates to pay for the replacement of social housing. On this reading, social housing in Waterloo depends on the same land value that the global-city frame creates, so it is difficult for it to act as a counterweight to that frame. This is an interpretation drawn from documents that I have read, and not a statement found in them. If it is right, the contradiction is built into the funding of the policy, which explains why the promise of mixing and the promise of return carry so much weight in deciding who bears the cost of the transplanted model.

en: The argument about a transplanted model can be tested, and it is useful to say what would change it. If most relocated tenants returned to the same place within a stated period, the promise of return would be shown to hold, and the cost to residents would be mostly the cost of waiting. If research on Green Square's own residents found that they too feel unheard or unsettled, the contrast between a place told as potential and a place told as a problem would have to be redrawn. Each possibility is open, and none can be settled with the documents read here. They are the reason that the conclusions are stated as interpretations consistent with the evidence, and not as findings about the two stories.

q: 五条建议你是否都同意？哪一条你想删或改？
en: Several planning implications follow from the argument that the cost of a transplanted model falls on residents, and each can be checked against the documents. First, the return promise should be defined and reported: how many tenants return, when, and to the same place or only the same area. Second, the project should publish the share of social housing alongside the number of social homes, since the stock is rising while the share is falling. Third, when a precinct is used as a precedent, the planning documents should say what the precedent does not carry, which here is the difference between land that is empty and land that is a home. Fourth, renewal should consider retention and renovation where feasible; Zanardo et al. (2024) conclude that most of the existing buildings, with the possible exception of the slab blocks, could have their lives extended with relatively modest renovation. Fifth, policy language should avoid locating the problem in the place, which Sisson (2024) criticises, and should give residents a voice, given that only a third of surveyed tenants feel heard (South Sydney Herald, 2024). These suggestions follow from the argument, and none of them requires the claim that the policy is acting in bad faith. Each recommendation answers a concept: the return promise answers emplaced displacement, the reported share answers residualisation, the explicit precedent answers the distinction between building and dwelling, retention answers new-build gentrification, and the choice of language answers territorial stigma. They ask only that the cost to residents be counted.

q: 局限段落很实，但读者可能想知道哪个局限最重要，你要不要排序？
en: The limits of the essay define how far the argument about the two stories can be pressed. I found no evidence on the experience of Green Square's residents or on how Green Square was regarded before redevelopment, so the contrast rests on official descriptions. Suburb-level census figures cannot show the difference between the estate's residents and those of the new apartments: in 2021 Waterloo and Zetland had similar median weekly household incomes (A$2,028 and A$2,192) and similar shares of rented dwellings (72.7 and 70.5 per cent), because the Waterloo suburb includes many private apartments (Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2021a, 2021b). I read only parts of the urban design study, and the 2023 tenant survey is known through a press report. Future work should read the whole design study, analyse the estate at a finer geography, and follow the relocation and return of tenants as they happen. Several concepts could not be tested here: indirect displacement, the subsidy gap, and neighbourhood effects at the level of the estate, because the data they need are not in the documents I read. Even so, the main point holds within these limits: when Waterloo is measured against Green Square, the measure leaves out the people who live there.
zh: 本文的局限决定了关于两个故事的论证能推进多远。我没有找到关于 Green Square 居民体验、或 Green Square 改造前如何被看待的证据，所以对比建立在官方描述之上。郊区层级的人口普查数据无法显示公屋区居民与新建公寓居民之间的差别：2021 年 Waterloo 与 Zetland 的家庭周收入中位数相近（2,028 澳元和 2,192 澳元），租住比例也相近（72.7% 和 70.5%），因为 Waterloo 这个郊区包含许多私人公寓（Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2021a, 2021b）。我只读了城市设计研究的部分内容，2023 年租户调查是通过媒体报道知道的。未来的工作应读完整份设计研究，在更精细的地理单位上分析公屋区，并在租户搬迁和回迁发生时跟踪它们。有几个概念在这里无法检验：间接置换、补贴差距，以及公屋区层面的邻里效应，因为它们所需的数据不在我读过的文件里。即便如此，主要的结论在这些局限之内依然成立：当用 Green Square 来衡量 Waterloo 时，这把尺子漏掉了住在那里的人。

q: 最后一句有“重复同样的模式”这样的预测，你要不要换成更克制的表述？
en: The essay therefore ends with a question that reframes the original one: what does the Green Square precedent leave out? The usual question is whether Waterloo should become more like Green Square, and the answer depends on what is counted. This essay's answer is the residents, their attachment to the place, and the years in which they wait. Seen in this way, the comparison is not an argument against redevelopment, nor does it argue that Green Square is a failure; it is an argument for including in the measure of a good urban place the people who already live in it. This is the point at which Sennett's distinction between building and dwelling, which no previous study of Waterloo examined, returns: a city is built for its economy, and it is dwelt in by its residents, and a planning model that counts only the first will repeat the pattern each time it is applied.
zh: 因此，本文以一个重新界定原问题的问题收尾：Green Square 这个先例遗漏了什么？通常的问题是 Waterloo 是否应当更像 Green Square，答案取决于计入什么。本文的答案是：居民、他们对这个地方的依恋，以及他们等待的那些年。这样看，这一对比既不是反对再开发的论证，也不是说 Green Square 是失败的；它主张的是，在衡量一个好的城市地方时，把已经住在那里的人也计入。这正是 Sennett 对“建造”与“栖居”的区分重新出现的地方——此前关于 Waterloo 的研究都没有考察过这一区分：城市是为它的经济而建的，也是由它的居民栖居的，一个只计入前者的规划模式，每次被应用时都会重复同样的模式。
